chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad and al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Ubayd ibn Zurarah, from Abi Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:
“The diyyah is one thousand dinars, or twelve thousand dirhams, or one hundred camels.” And he said: “If you strike a man with a piece of iron, then that is intentional killing.”

key_terms.الْإِبِلِ: camels, given here as another standard measure for diyyah
key_terms.الْعَمْدُ: intentional act, meaning deliberate killing in this context
key_terms.اَلدِّيَةُ: financial compensation due for unlawful killing or injury
key_terms.بِحَدِيدَةٍ: with an iron instrument or piece of iron
key_terms.دِرْهَمٍ: a silver coin used here as an alternative legal measure of diyyah
key_terms.دِينَارٍ: a gold coin used here as a legal measure of diyyah

ai.seo_question: What is the amount of diyyah, and when is a killing considered intentional in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith states the legally recognized amounts for diyyah and clarifies that striking a person with iron is treated as intentional harm. It is significant in fiqh because it defines compensation standards and helps distinguish deliberate killing from other categories.
